# Reference models

Models whose answer is known exactly, from a formula found in the textbooks of the subject, beside what the engine gives when it runs them. Every model here is one of the [bundled models](gallery/index.md), so each line can be repeated with one command.

| Case | Method | Model | Quantity | Exact | Naga | 95% interval | Exact inside | Replications | Seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| M/G/1 queue (Pollaczek-Khinchine) | Discrete-event | `single_server_general` | mean number waiting | 1.9 | 1.88 | 1.78 to 1.98 | yes | 20 | 0 |

## How to read it

**Exact** is the formula's value, computed from the parameters in the model file. **Naga** is the mean over the replications of a run made when this page was generated, and the interval is its 95% Student-t confidence interval over those replications. Numbers are printed at three significant digits; "inside" is decided before rounding.

A 95% interval misses the true value one time in twenty by chance. 6 lines here have an interval, so a "no" somewhere in the table is expected for about one seed in 4, with nothing wrong. Where a line has no interval, the model has no randomness and the two numbers are compared as printed.

The intervals are a few percent wide because the runs are kept to a few seconds each. An interval narrows with the square root of the simulated time: give a command below a longer `--run-length` or more `--replications` to see it close in on the exact value.

`tools/gen_engine_docs.py` makes the runs and writes this page; no number on it is typed. A test derives each value a second way (the Markov chain summed state by state, or the differential equation integrated numerically), repeats each run, and fails when the exact value is outside the interval or when a line here is not what the run gives.

## The cases

### M/M/1 queue

Single server (M/M/1) (`single_server`), mean number waiting: the KPI `resource/Server/Queue Length Avg`.

Exact: Lq = rho^2 / (1 - rho), rho = lambda / mu.

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run single_server --replications 20 --run-length 10500 --warmup 500
```

### M/M/2 queue (Erlang C)

Two tellers (resource set) (`two_teller_set`), mean number waiting: the KPI `resource/Tellers/Queue Length Avg`.

Exact: Lq = p0 a^c rho / (c! (1 - rho)^2), a = lambda / mu, rho = a / c, 1 / p0 = sum over n < c of a^n / n! + a^c / (c! (1 - rho)).

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run two_teller_set --replications 20 --run-length 5500 --warmup 500
```

### M/G/1 queue (Pollaczek-Khinchine)

Single server, general service times (M/G/1) (`single_server_general`), mean number waiting: the KPI `resource/Server/Queue Length Avg`.

Exact: Lq = lambda^2 E[S^2] / (2 (1 - rho)), rho = lambda E[S].

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run single_server_general
```

### Open Jackson network

Job shop (Jackson network) (`job_shop_jackson`), mean time in the shop: the KPI `system/Avg Throughput Time`.

Exact: W = sum of L_i / gamma: station i an M/M/c queue at the rate lambda_i of the traffic equations lambda_i = gamma_i + sum over j of lambda_j p_ji, L_i = Lq_i + lambda_i / mu_i.

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run job_shop_jackson --replications 10 --run-length 6500 --warmup 500
```

### Logistic growth

Population (logistic) (`sd_population`), population at t = 25: the KPI `level/population_1/SD Population/Final`.

Exact: P(t) = K / (1 + (K / P0 - 1) exp(-r t)).

```console
naga run sd_population --run-length 25
```

### Bass diffusion

Bass diffusion (`sd_bass_diffusion`), adopters at t = 10: the KPI `level/bass_diffusion_1/SD Adopters/Final`.

Exact: A(t) = m (1 - exp(-(p + q) t)) / (1 + (q / p) exp(-(p + q) t)).

```console
naga run sd_bass_diffusion --run-length 10
```

### SIR epidemic

SIR epidemic (`sd_sir`), peak number infected: the KPI `level/sir_1/SD Infected/Max`.

Exact: I_max = N - rho (1 + ln(S0 / rho)), rho = gamma N / beta.

```console
naga run sd_sir
```

### Busy/idle cycle

Server busy/idle cycle (agents) (`agents_server_utilization`), share of the time busy: the KPI `agent/server_utilization_1/Servers/Busy/Avg Count`.

Exact: lambda / (lambda + mu).

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run agents_server_utilization --replications 10
```

### SIR epidemic of agents

SIR epidemic (agents) (`agents_sir_agents`), final number recovered: the KPI `agent/sir_agents_1/SIR People/R/Final`.

Exact: the mean of N - S when the last infected agent recovers, summed over every path of the Markov chain: from (S, I) the next event is an infection with probability beta S / (beta S + gamma N), else a recovery.

<!-- no-run: takes several seconds; a test of its own repeats this run -->
```console
naga run agents_sir_agents --replications 20 --run-length 300
```

### Tank, average level

Tank: fill, overflow and run dry (`tank_fill_and_drain`), time-average level: the KPI `level/Tank/Average`.

Exact: the area under three straight lines (rise to full, full, fall to empty) over the run.

```console
naga run tank_fill_and_drain
```

### Tank, overflow

Tank: fill, overflow and run dry (`tank_fill_and_drain`), quantity spilled: the KPI `level/Tank/Spilled`.

Exact: (fill - draw) x the time the tank is full while the pump runs.

The same run as the line above.

## What this does not show

Agreement on these cases says the engine's clock, queues, random streams, integrators and statistics are right where a formula can check them. It says nothing about a model that has no formula, which is most models: for those, see [Model assertions](model-assertions.md) and [Experiments](experiments.md).
